column1: Tavilo competitor-user research v3 - workbook built 2026-10-07
TABS
1. Prospects - start here: 501 companies with strong evidence they use a competitor, ranked. Work top to bottom. Use the Owner / Outreach status / Notes columns at the right to track outreach.
Tier A (200): named decision maker with a direct route, 11-2,500 staff, and complaints about their current tool or priority score 50+.
Tier B (247): named decision maker with a direct route.
Tier C (54): only a company phone, email or LinkedIn. Find the decision maker first.
Left out: No contact found yet (80); Uses a clock-in app for hourly/field staff (25); Too large (over 2,500 staff) (19). They are still in the Strong evidence tab.
2. Unhappy customers: 107 company + tool pairs where a company complained about a tool or switched away from it. 'Unhappy with (tool)' names the tool that caused it.
Hubstaff 26, Harvest 22, Time Doctor 10, Unnamed previous tool 7, ActivTrak 6, ProHance 5, Jibble 4, Toggl Track 3, DeskTime 3, Clockify 3 (targetable rows).
3. Strong evidence - all: all 625 CURRENT or PROBABLE companies, including those left out of the prospect list and why.
4. Needs validation: 946 POSSIBLE companies (weak or ambiguous evidence, mostly technographic). Do not cold-pitch as users.
5. Former customers: 45 rows where a company stopped using a tool.
6. Do not target: 623 companies ruled out (vendor, false match, defunct, no evidence). Reason in Notes.
7. Competitor summary / Competitor pricing / Channel summary / Source audit: reference tables.
8. Master (all rows): all 2290 company + tool rows with every field.
DEFINITIONS
CURRENT = strong recent evidence they use the tool. PROBABLE = strong but not fully confirmed. POSSIBLE = weak/ambiguous. FORMER = a source says they stopped. DO_NOT_TARGET = ruled out.
Confidence (0-100) = how sure we are they use the tool. Priority score (0-100) = how good a Tavilo prospect they are.
Seats, costs and savings are ESTIMATES from list prices. When no seat count was stated, seats = headcount.
CONTACT RULES

Every name, LinkedIn, phone and email was copied from a public page (see Contact source). Nothing was guessed: no email was built from a name pattern and no LinkedIn URL was constructed. Blank = not found.
Anonymous reviewers were never identified. 'Who said it = Employees' means the complaint came from staff reviews, not management: use it as a privacy/morale angle, never quote or name the reviewer.
Contacts can go stale. Check the person is still in the role before reaching out.
